subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested locally H^n-finite Borel sets
subproblems.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and A ⊆ B ⊆ U Borel sets with H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (H^n = μHE[n]). Then for H^n⌞A-a.e. x, simultaneously for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q) if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–3 and 6 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4, Remarks 1.5(2)–(3) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒", chapter-03.txt lines 77–143), in the general form needed for an equivalence. The parent obtains the growth bound of the smaller set A = F(B) from the bi-Lipschitz estimate of its step 3. Here it is derived from the tangent plane itself (step 5 below, the quantitative content of Simon's Remark 1.5(3)), so that both implications hold off one null set and no bi-Lipschitz hypothesis is needed. In the parent this child is applied with (U, A, B) := (U, F(B), Y): A = F(B) is Borel by the piece_pullback child, F(B) ⊆ Y ⊆ U, and Y is locally H^n-finite in U. Definition used: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q means finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0) for every f ∈ C_c(E). The integrals are Bochner integrals, and a non-integrable integrand gives 0. Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n]; B̄_ρ(z), B_ρ(z) are the closed and open balls; η_{x,r}(z) := r^{-1}(z − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r); I_r(S) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dH^n for a fixed f ∈ C_c(E).
1. Blow-up scaling. Let r > 0, R > 0 and S ⊆ E. Since |η_{x,r}(z)| = r^{-1}|z − x|, we have η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B̄_R(0) = η_{x,r}(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)). Also H^n(η_{x,r}(T)) = r^{-n} H^n(T) for every T ⊆ E: η_{x,r} is the homothety AffineMap.homothety x r^{-1} followed by the translation z ↦ z − x. The homothety multiplies μHE[n] by ‖r^{-1}‖₊^n = r^{-n} (MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), and the translation is an isometry, so it preserves μHE[n] (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Hence H^n(η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)). Moreover η_{x,r} is a homeomorphism of E (inverse w ↦ x + rw), so it is injective and maps Borel sets to Borel sets. In particular η_{x,r}(B) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets η_{x,r}(A) and η_{x,r}(B ∖ A).
2. Countable cover. Let D ⊆ E be a countable dense set. Let 𝒦 be the countable family of closed balls B̄_s(q) with q ∈ D, s ∈ ℚ, s > 0 and B̄_s(q) ⊆ U. Every z ∈ U lies in the open ball B_s(q) of some member: choose δ > 0 with B_δ(z) ⊆ U, then q ∈ D with |z − q| < δ/4 and a rational s ∈ (δ/4, δ/2). Then |z − q| < s, and B̄_s(q) ⊆ B_δ(z) because s + δ/4 < δ. Each K ∈ 𝒦 is compact (closed and bounded in the finite-dimensional space E) with K ⊆ U, so H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞. If U = ∅ then 𝒦 = ∅, A = ∅ and H^n⌞A = 0, so everything below is vacuous.
3. Besicovitch density. Fix K ∈ 𝒦 and let ν_K := H^n⌞(B ∩ K). It is a finite, hence locally finite, Borel measure on E. E is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so it is second countable and has the Besicovitch covering property. By the Besicovitch density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div applied to ν_K and A), for ν_K⌞A-a.e. z the ratio ν_K(A ∩ B̄_ρ(z))/ν_K(B̄_ρ(z)) in [0, ∞] tends to 1 as ρ → 0⁺. Call this property Conv_K(z). Since A, B and K are Borel and A ⊆ B, ν_K⌞A = H^n⌞(A ∩ K) = (H^n⌞A)⌞K. So for H^n⌞A-a.e. z, z ∈ K implies Conv_K(z). Since 𝒦 is countable and A is Borel, there is an H^n⌞A-null set N such that every z ∉ N satisfies z ∈ A and Conv_K(z) for every K ∈ 𝒦 with z ∈ K. N does not depend on any subspace Q.
4. Relative smallness of the excess. Fix x ∉ N. Since x ∈ A ⊆ U, choose K = B̄_s(q) ∈ 𝒦 with |x − q| < s and put ρ₀ := s − |x − q| > 0. Then B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ K for 0 < ρ < ρ₀. Write a(ρ) := H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)), β(ρ) := H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) and e(ρ) := H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). For 0 < ρ < ρ₀:
- ν_K(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = a(ρ);
- ν_K(B̄_ρ(x)) = β(ρ) ≤ H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞;
- β(ρ) = a(ρ) + e(ρ), by additivity on the disjoint Borel sets A ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and (B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x).
Also H^n(B ∩ B̄_{ρ₀/2}(x)) ≤ H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞.
Claim: for every ε > 0 there is ρ_ε ∈ (0, ρ₀] with e(ρ) ≤ ε β(ρ) for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ_ε).
- If ε ≥ 1, take ρ_ε := ρ₀, since e ≤ β.
- If 0 < ε < 1, Conv_K(x) gives ρ_ε ∈ (0, ρ₀] with a(ρ)/β(ρ) > 1 − ε for 0 < ρ < ρ_ε. Then a(ρ) > 0, because a zero numerator makes the quotient 0. Hence 0 < β(ρ) < ∞ and a(ρ) > (1 − ε) β(ρ), that is, e(ρ) = β(ρ) − a(ρ) < ε β(ρ).
5. Growth from a tangent plane. Let S ⊆ E be Borel and r₀ > 0 with H^n(S ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞, and suppose S has approximate tangent space Q at x. Then there are C ≥ 0 and r₁ > 0 with H^n(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C ρ^n for all ρ ∈ (0, r₁). Proof:
- Let φ(w) := max(0, min(1, 2 − |w|)). It is continuous with tsupport φ ⊆ B̄_2(0), which is compact (isCompact_closedBall), so φ defines an element of C_c(E, ℝ). Also 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on B̄_1(0) and φ = 0 off B̄_2(0).
- For 0 < ρ ≤ r₀/2, step 1 gives H^n(η_{x,ρ}(S) ∩ B̄_2(0)) = ρ^{-n} H^n(S ∩ B̄_{2ρ}(x)) < ∞. So φ is H^n-integrable on η_{x,ρ}(S), and ρ^{-n} H^n(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = H^n(η_{x,ρ}(S) ∩ B̄_1(0)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(S)} φ dH^n.
- The right side tends to Λ := ∫_Q φ dH^n. Hence there is r₁ ∈ (0, r₀/2] such that it is ≤ |Λ| + 1 for 0 < ρ < r₁. Take C := |Λ| + 1.
6. Zero n-density of the excess. Let x ∉ N with ρ₀ as in step 4, and suppose a(ρ) ≤ C ρ^n for all ρ ∈ (0, r₁), where C ≥ 0 and r₁ > 0. Then ρ^{-n} e(ρ) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺.
- Step 4 with ε = 1/2 gives β(ρ) = a(ρ) + e(ρ) ≤ a(ρ) + β(ρ)/2 with β(ρ) < ∞. So β(ρ) ≤ 2a(ρ) ≤ 2Cρ^n for 0 < ρ < min(ρ_{1/2}, r₁).
- Given δ > 0, step 4 with ε := δ/(2C + 1) gives e(ρ) ≤ ε β(ρ) ≤ δ ρ^n for 0 < ρ < min(ρ_ε, ρ_{1/2}, r₁).
7. Transfer of blow-up limits. Let x ∉ N with ρ₀ as in step 4, and suppose ρ^{-n} e(ρ) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺. Then for every f ∈ C_c(E), I_r(B) − I_r(A) → 0 as r → 0⁺. Proof:
- Choose R > 0 with f = 0 off B̄_R(0) (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded) and M ≥ 0 with |f| ≤ M.
- For 0 < r ≤ ρ₀/(2R), step 1 gives H^n(η_{x,r}(B) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(B ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)) ≤ r^{-n} H^n(B ∩ B̄_{ρ₀/2}(x)) < ∞.
- f is continuous, |f| ≤ M and f = 0 off B̄_R(0). So f is H^n-integrable on η_{x,r}(B) and on its Borel subsets η_{x,r}(A) and η_{x,r}(B ∖ A).
- By additivity over the disjoint union of step 1, I_r(B) − I_r(A) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(B∖A)} f dH^n. Its absolute value is at most M H^n(η_{x,r}(B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = M r^{-n} e(rR) = M R^n (rR)^{-n} e(rR).
- As r → 0⁺, rR → 0⁺, so this bound tends to 0. For n = 0 all these powers equal 1.
8. Conclusion. Let x ∉ N, with K and ρ₀ as in step 4, and let Q be a linear subspace of E. Note that a ≤ β (since A ⊆ B) and H^n(A ∩ B̄_{ρ₀/2}(x)) ≤ H^n(B ∩ B̄_{ρ₀/2}(x)) < ∞.
(⇒) Suppose B has approximate tangent space Q at x.
- Step 5 with S := B and r₀ := ρ₀/2 gives C and r₁ with a(ρ) ≤ β(ρ) ≤ Cρ^n for ρ ∈ (0, r₁).
- By steps 6 and 7, I_r(A) = I_r(B) − (I_r(B) − I_r(A)) → ∫_Q f dH^n for every f ∈ C_c(E).
- Together with finrank Q = n, A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
(⇐) Suppose A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
- Step 5 with S := A and r₀ := ρ₀/2 gives a(ρ) ≤ Cρ^n for ρ ∈ (0, r₁).
- By steps 6 and 7, I_r(B) = I_r(A) + (I_r(B) − I_r(A)) → ∫_Q f dH^n for every f ∈ C_c(E).
- Together with finrank Q = n, B has approximate tangent space Q at x.
N is H^n⌞A-null and independent of Q. So the equivalence holds for H^n⌞A-a.e. x, simultaneously for all Q. ∎
Reuse note (not used above): this exact frozen type is already comparator-accepted as Submission.ptd_ae_approxTangent_iff_of_subset (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.piece_tangent_density-a1.tangent_locality-a1, candidate commit 0a7763279333fcd94fa0f753fabf75cc0ad1a1fb), whose Lean proof follows steps 1–8 above. proof_key_steps: Blow-up scaling H^n(η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = r^{-n} H^n(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)), and η_{x,r}(B) is the disjoint Borel union of η_{x,r}(A) and η_{x,r}(B ∖ A).
Cover U by countably many open balls whose closures are compact subsets of U.
Apply Besicovitch density to H^n⌞(B ∩ K) on each ball; this gives one H^n⌞A-null exceptional set N, independent of Q.
Off N, H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ε H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for all small ρ.
A tangent plane of B or of A at x gives H^n(· ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ Cρ^n (cutoff test function).
So ∫_{η(B)} f − ∫_{η(A)} f → 0 for every f ∈ C_c, giving the equivalence for all Q at once.

subproblems.title: Borel image and null-set pullback along a bi-Lipschitz piece
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for all a, a' ∈ B. Then F(B) is Borel. Moreover, for every predicate p on ℝ^P that holds H^n⌞F(B)-a.e. (H^n = μHE[n]), p(F(b)) holds for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B, i.e. (volume.restrict B)-a.e.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → MeasurableSet (F '' B) ∧ ∀ p : Euclid P → Prop, (∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n].restrict (F '' B)), p y) → ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), p (F b)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0(a)–(b) of the parent proof (and the null-set transfer N₃ := G(N₁ ∩ A) of its step 6). In the parent this child is applied to (F, B, L, m) and to the predicate p(y) := ∀ Q, (Y has approximate tangent space Q at y ↔ F(B) has approximate tangent space Q at y). Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E and on ℝ^n; λ := volume on ℝ^n. On ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = λ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. F is injective on B. If a, a' ∈ B and F(a) = F(a'), then m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| = 0, and m > 0 gives a = a'.
2. F(B) is Borel. F is continuous (Lipschitz), ℝ^n is Polish, B is Borel and F is injective on B. So F(B) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
3. Inverse map. Let G := Function.invFunOn F B : E → ℝ^n. For y ∈ F(B), G(y) ∈ B and F(G(y)) = y (invFunOn_pos). For y, y' ∈ F(B), m|G(y) − G(y')| ≤ |F(G(y)) − F(G(y'))| = |y − y'|. So G is m^{-1}-Lipschitz on F(B), that is, LipschitzOnWith (Real.toNNReal m^{-1}) G (F '' B). The Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, valid between any two metric spaces with their Borel σ-algebras) gives μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ (m^{-1})^n μHE[n](S) for every S ⊆ F(B).
4. Pullback. Let p be a predicate on E with p(y) for H^n⌞F(B)-a.e. y.
- F(B) is measurable by step 2. So, by ae_restrict_iff', H^n-a.e. y satisfies y ∈ F(B) → p(y). That is, S := {y : y ∈ F(B) ∧ ¬p(y)} is H^n-null.
- Let T := {b : b ∈ B ∧ ¬p(F(b))}. If b ∈ T then y := F(b) ∈ S. Also G(y) ∈ B and F(G(y)) = F(b), so G(y) = b by step 1. Hence T ⊆ G(S).
- By step 3 and μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n, λ(T) ≤ μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ (m^{-1})^n · 0 = 0.
- Since B is measurable, ae_restrict_iff' turns λ(T) = 0 into: p(F(b)) holds for (volume.restrict B)-a.e. b. ∎
For n = 0 every power is 1 and the argument is unchanged.

This decomposition reuses that declaration with the identical type, so no new formalization is required.
proof_key_steps: The lower bound m|a − a'| ≤ |F a − F a'| makes F injective on B.
G := invFunOn F B is m⁻¹-Lipschitz on F(B); the Lipschitz image bound gives μHE[n](G(S)) ≤ m^{-n} μHE[n](S).
The bad parameters {b ∈ B : ¬p(F b)} lie in G of the H^n-null bad image set; μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n, and ae_restrict_iff' concludes.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of a bi-Lipschitz Lipschitz image
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for a, a' ∈ B. Suppose F is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B, F(B) has approximate tangent space range DF(b) at F(b): HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (range DF(b)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ F a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ F a)) → ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F b : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0, 3 (growth bound), 4, 5 and 7 of the parent proof. Here the conclusion is stated for F(B) itself; the comparison with Y in steps 1–3 and 6 is a separate child. Definition used: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y Q means finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0) for every f ∈ C_c(E). Notation:
- E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E or on ℝ^n; λ := volume on ℝ^n (= μHE[n] there, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume);
- A := F(B); B̄_r(z) and B_r(z) are the closed and open balls; η_{y,r}(z) := r^{-1}(z − y) (SimonGMT blowUpMap y r);
- J(a) := normDet(DF(a)) (= SimonGMT areaJacobianAt F a); L_b := DF(b); ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|;
- ω_n := λ(B̄_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞), so λ(B̄_t(z)) = ω_n t^n for t ≥ 0 (Measure.addHaar_closedBall', finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n).
0. Preliminaries.
(a) F is injective on B: if F(a) = F(a') with a, a' ∈ B then m|a − a'| ≤ 0, and m > 0. F is also continuous. So A is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; ℝ^n is Polish).
(b) Lipschitz images: H^n(F(S)) ≤ L^n H^n(S) = L^n λ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^n (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).
(c) Growth: let b ∈ B and s > 0. If a ∈ B and F(a) ∈ B̄_s(F(b)), then m|a − b| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| ≤ s. So A ∩ B̄_s(F(b)) ⊆ F(B̄_{s/m}(b)), and by (b), H^n(A ∩ B̄_s(F(b))) ≤ L^n ω_n m^{-n} s^n.
(d) Scaling: let r > 0. η_{y,r} is the homothety with centre y and ratio r^{-1} followed by the translation z ↦ z − y. So H^n(η_{y,r}(S)) = r^{-n} H^n(S) for every S ⊆ E (MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image, Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
- η_{y,r} is a homeomorphism (inverse w ↦ y + rw), hence a measurable embedding that maps Borel sets to Borel sets, and |η_{y,r}(z)| < R ⇔ |z − y| < rR.
- For Borel S, the image of H^n⌞S under η_{y,r} is r^n·H^n⌞η_{y,r}(S): for Borel T, H^n(S ∩ η_{y,r}^{-1}(T)) = r^n H^n(η_{y,r}(S) ∩ T).
- In Lean form: Measure.map η_{y,r} (μHE[n].restrict S) = ENNReal.ofReal (r^n) • μHE[n].restrict (η_{y,r} '' S). Hence ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} g dH^n = r^{-n} ∫_S g(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z) for every Borel g : E → ℝ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, integral_smul_measure). No integrability is needed: if one side is not integrable, neither is the other, and both integrals are 0.
(e) Jacobian: J is Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt) and 0 ≤ J(a) ≤ L^n for every a.
- ‖DF(a)‖ ≤ L by norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; DF(a) = 0 where F is not differentiable.
- For every linear T : ℝ^n → E, normDet(T)·ω_n = H^n(T(B̄_1(0))) ≤ ‖T‖^n ω_n. The equality is LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume. The inequality is euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn for the ‖T‖-Lipschitz map T (T.lipschitz), together with μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n.
- Since ω_n ∈ (0, ∞), normDet(T) ≤ ‖T‖^n.
(f) Area formula: ∫⁻_A g dH^n = ∫⁻_B J(a) g(F(a)) dλ(a) for every g : E → [0, ∞]. This is SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn with s = B, using (a) and finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n.
1. Good parameters. Two theorems apply to λ:
- the Lebesgue density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for λ and B);
- the Lebesgue differentiation theorem, applied to J, which is bounded and Borel, hence locally integrable. Use IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub with μ := volume (doubling by the instance isUnifLocDoublingMeasureOfIsAddHaarMeasure), K := 1, ι := ℝ, l := 𝓝[>] 0, w := fun _ ↦ b and δ := id; the side condition b ∈ B̄_ρ(b) is trivial, and the radii tend to 0⁺ by self_mem_nhdsWithin.
So λ-a.e. b ∈ B satisfies:
(α) λ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(b))/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺. Since λ(B̄_ρ(b)) = ω_n ρ^n ∈ (0, ∞), equivalently ρ^{-n} λ(B̄_ρ(b) ∖ B) → 0.
(β) ⨍_{B̄_ρ(b)} |J(a) − J(b)| dλ(a) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺, equivalently ρ^{-n} ∫_{B̄_ρ(b)} |J(a) − J(b)| dλ(a) → 0.
The set of b ∈ B satisfying (α) and (β) is (volume.restrict B)-conull and does not depend on any test function. Fix such b. F is differentiable at b by hypothesis. Put y := F(b) and L_b := DF(b).
2. Lower bound (γ): m|c| ≤ |L_b c| for every c ∈ ℝ^n.
- This is trivial for c = 0. Let c ≠ 0, so n ≥ 1 and ℝ^n is nontrivial, and let δ ∈ (0, |c|).
- For r > 0 the open ball W_r := B_{rδ}(b + rc) satisfies W_r ⊆ B̄_{r(|c|+δ)}(b) and λ(W_r) = ω_n (rδ)^n (open and closed balls have equal measure, Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball).
- If W_r ∩ B = ∅, then with ρ := r(|c| + δ), λ(B̄_ρ(b) ∖ B)/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) ≥ (δ/(|c| + δ))^n > 0. By (α) this ratio tends to 0, so there is r_δ > 0 with W_r ∩ B ≠ ∅ for all r ∈ (0, r_δ).
- Let θ > 0. Differentiability at b gives ρ_θ > 0 with |F(b + h) − F(b) − L_b h| ≤ θ|h| whenever |h| < ρ_θ.
- Choose r ∈ (0, r_δ) with r(|c| + δ) < ρ_θ, and c' with |c' − c| < δ and b + rc' ∈ B. Since b and b + rc' lie in B, m r|c'| ≤ |F(b + rc') − F(b)| ≤ r|L_b c'| + θ r|c'|. So m|c'| ≤ |L_b c'| + θ|c'|.
- Using |c| − δ ≤ |c'| ≤ |c| + δ and |L_b c'| ≤ |L_b c| + ‖L_b‖δ gives m(|c| − δ) ≤ |L_b c| + ‖L_b‖δ + θ(|c| + δ).
- This holds for every θ > 0 and δ ∈ (0, |c|). Letting θ → 0 and then δ → 0 gives m|c| ≤ |L_b c|.
Consequently L_b is injective and finrank(range L_b) = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj).
3. Setup. Fix f ∈ C_c(E). Choose R > 0 with f(w) = 0 whenever |w| ≥ R (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded). Let M := ‖f‖_∞ < ∞ and D := B̄_{R/m}(0) ⊆ ℝ^n. For r > 0 and c ∈ ℝ^n let Φ_r(c) := (F(b + rc) − F(b))/r.
4. Rescaled area formula. For every r > 0, f is H^n-integrable on η_{y,r}(A) and
∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc) J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c).
(i) η_{y,r}(A) is Borel. Also η_{y,r}(A) ∩ B_R(0) = η_{y,r}(A ∩ B_{rR}(y)), which has H^n-measure r^{-n} H^n(A ∩ B_{rR}(y)) ≤ L^n ω_n (R/m)^n < ∞ by 0(c) and 0(d). Since f is Borel, |f| ≤ M and f = 0 off B_R(0), f is integrable on η_{y,r}(A).
(ii) By 0(d), ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n = r^{-n} ∫_A g dH^n with g := f∘η_{y,r}. g is Borel, |g| ≤ M and g = 0 off B_{rR}(y).
(iii) Apply 0(f) to the weights g⁺ := max(g, 0), g⁻ := max(−g, 0) and |g|.
- ∫⁻_A g^± dH^n = ∫⁻_B J(a) g^±(F(a)) dλ(a), and ∫⁻_B J(a)|g(F(a))| dλ(a) = ∫⁻_A |g| dH^n ≤ M H^n(A ∩ B_{rR}(y)) < ∞.
- So a ↦ 1_B(a) J(a) g(F(a)) is Borel and λ-integrable. As J ≥ 0, its positive and negative parts are a ↦ 1_B(a) J(a) g^±(F(a)).
- Write both Bochner integrals as differences of the lintegrals of their positive and negative parts (integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part). This gives ∫_A g dH^n = ∫_B J(a) g(F(a)) dλ(a).
(iv) Substitute a = b + rc. λ is translation invariant and ∫ h(rc) dλ(c) = r^{-n} ∫ h dλ for r > 0 (Measure.integral_comp_smul). Using (F(b + rc) − y)/r = Φ_r(c), this gives ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(a) J(a) f((F(a) − y)/r) dλ(a) = r^n ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc) J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c). Combining (ii)–(iv) proves the formula.
5. Localisation.
- If b + rc ∈ B and f(Φ_r(c)) ≠ 0, then |Φ_r(c)| < R. So m r|c| ≤ |F(b + rc) − F(b)| < rR, and |c| < R/m.
- If f(L_b c) ≠ 0 then |L_b c| < R, and by (γ), |c| < R/m.
Hence the integrand of step 4 and c ↦ J(b) f(L_b c) both vanish outside D, and I_∞ := ∫_{ℝ^n} J(b) f(L_b c) dλ(c) = ∫_D J(b) f(L_b c) dλ(c).
6. Convergence: ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n → I_∞ as r → 0⁺.
- Let c ∈ D. Add and subtract J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) and J(b) f(Φ_r(c)), and use 0 ≤ J ≤ L^n and |f| ≤ M:
|1_B(b + rc) J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) − J(b) f(L_b c)| ≤ L^n M 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc) + M|J(b + rc) − J(b)| + J(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)|.
- All three terms are bounded Borel functions of c, D has finite measure ω_n (R/m)^n, and both integrands vanish off D by step 5. So |∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n − I_∞| is at most the integral over D of the right-hand side.
(i) ∫_D 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc) dλ(c) = r^{-n} λ(B̄_{rR/m}(b) ∖ B) = (R/m)^n · s^{-n} λ(B̄_s(b) ∖ B) with s := rR/m → 0⁺. This tends to 0 by (α).
(ii) ∫_D |J(b + rc) − J(b)| dλ(c) = r^{-n} ∫_{B̄_{rR/m}(b)} |J(a) − J(b)| dλ(a) = (R/m)^n · s^{-n} ∫_{B̄_s(b)} |J − J(b)| dλ. This tends to 0 by (β).
(iii) Given θ > 0, let ρ_θ be as in step 2. For 0 < r < ρ_θ m/R and c ∈ D we have |rc| < ρ_θ, so |Φ_r(c) − L_b c| = r^{-1}|F(b + rc) − F(b) − L_b(rc)| ≤ θ|c| ≤ θR/m. Thus Φ_r → L_b uniformly on D. Since f is uniformly continuous (CompactlySupportedContinuousMapClass.uniformContinuous), sup_{c ∈ D} |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)| → 0. Hence ∫_D J(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)| dλ(c) ≤ J(b) λ(D) sup_D |…| → 0.
Hence ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n → I_∞.
7. Identification: I_∞ = ∫_{range L_b} f dH^n.
- By LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume (finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n), H^n(L_b(S)) = normDet(L_b) λ(S) = J(b) λ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^n.
- For Borel T ⊆ E, L_b(L_b^{-1}(T)) = range L_b ∩ T, so H^n(range L_b ∩ T) = J(b) λ(L_b^{-1}(T)). That is, H^n⌞range L_b is the image measure of J(b)·λ under L_b (range L_b is closed, hence Borel).
- L_b is an injective linear map between finite-dimensional spaces, hence a closed embedding (LinearMap.isClosedEmbedding_of_injective) and a measurable embedding. So MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure give ∫_{range L_b} f dH^n = J(b) ∫_{ℝ^n} f(L_b c) dλ(c) = I_∞.
8. Conclusion. By steps 4, 6 and 7, ∫_{η_{F(b),r}(F(B))} f dH^n → ∫_{range DF(b)} f dH^n as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(E), and finrank(range DF(b)) = n by step 2. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (range DF(b)) holds at every b ∈ B satisfying (α) and (β), that is, for (volume.restrict B)-a.e. b.
9. Dimension zero. For n = 0 the argument runs as written:
- ℝ^0 = {0} = D, B ⊆ {0}, ω_0 ∈ (0, ∞) and r^{±0} = 1;
- J ≡ 1 (LinearMap.normDet_of_subsingleton);
- (α) and (β) hold at b = 0 when 0 ∈ B, and (γ) concerns only c = 0;
- range L_b = {0} has finrank 0.
(Optional observation, not used: if n > P, no injective DF(a) exists, so B = ∅. Steps 0–8 need no case split, since (γ) already yields injectivity at good points.)
Imports: the Lean proof needs Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaApproximation (area formula, measurable_areaJacobianAt) and Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet. The submission may add these imports; the frozen statement does not use them. The statement mentions no Jacobian because LinearMap.normDet and areaJacobianAt are not in scope after import GMT.Ch07.Submission.

This decomposition reuses that declaration by name with the identical type, so no new formalization is required.
proof_key_steps: Preliminaries: F(B) is Borel; H^n(F(B) ∩ B̄_s(F b)) ≤ L^n ω_n m^{-n} s^n; H^n scales by r^{-n} under η_{y,r}; J = normDet DF is Borel with 0 ≤ J ≤ L^n; injective Lipschitz area formula on B.
For λ-a.e. b ∈ B: (α) b is a Lebesgue density point of B and (β) b is a Lebesgue point of J.
At such b, density plus differentiability give m|c| ≤ |DF(b)c| for all c.
Rescaled area formula: ∫_{η_{F b,r}(F(B))} f dH^n = ∫ 1_B(b+rc) J(b+rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c), with every integrand supported in B̄_{R/m}(0).
A three-term estimate using (α), (β) and the uniform convergence Φ_r → DF(b) on B̄_{R/m}(0) gives the limit J(b)∫ f(DF(b)c) dλ(c).
H^n(DF(b)S) = J(b)λ(S) identifies the limit with ∫_{range DF(b)} f dH^n, and finrank(range DF(b)) = n.
